page: Microsoft Azure FX24mds is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the FXMDVS server family. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance is specifically engineered for memory-intensive workloads, offering a substantial memory capacity of 504.0 GB, which translates to an exceptionally high ratio of 21.0 GB of RAM per core.

For storage, the FX24mds is equipped with a 1032 GB local SSD and is Premium Storage capable, enabling high-performance external disk attachments. The server does not include any integrated GPUs, making it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated graphics or GPU-based machine learning. Additionally, it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound applications. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require massive RAM footprints without needing a proportional increase in compute cores. The FX24mds is optimized for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, enterprise applications, and heavy data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure FX24mds is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the FXMDVS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor, it features 24 dedicated vCPUs and an extensive 504.0 GB of system memory, yielding 21.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes a 1032 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage for demanding I/O requirements, though it lacks integrated GPUs. This configuration is engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, such as large-scale relational databases, in-memory analytics, and heavy data processing, where high memory density is critical for performance. The high memory-to-CPU ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency by allowing organizations to run large datasets in memory without paying for unnecessary compute cores.
